$comment: THE single source of truth for every visual value in every client - React storefront, Angular storefront, both admin panels, and React Native. Nothing in an application may define a colour, a spacing step, or a font size of its own. See web/design-tokens/README.md and docs/adr/0014.
$schema-note: Plain data, deliberately. Defined as CSS it could never feed React Native, which has no stylesheet and no custom properties. Defined as data, build.mjs can generate whatever each platform needs.

color.$comment: SEMANTIC names, not literal ones. `surface-raised`, never `grey-100`: a literal name has to be renamed when the value changes, and in a dark theme `grey-100` becomes actively misleading. Every pair used for text-on-background is contrast-checked by build.mjs against WCAG 2.2 AA.

status.$comment: Status colours are never used alone to convey meaning - every status also carries an icon and a text label. Roughly 1 in 12 men has some colour vision deficiency, so colour-only status is unreadable for them and fails WCAG 1.4.1.

space.$comment: A 4px scale. Constraining spacing to a scale is what makes independently-built React and Angular screens line up pixel for pixel - with free-form values they never quite do.

family.sans: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
family.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

size.$comment: rem, not px, so the layout honours the browser's font-size setting. Fixed px text cannot be enlarged by a user who needs it larger, which fails WCAG 1.4.4.

breakpoint.$comment: Mobile-first: these are min-widths. Base styles target the smallest screen and each breakpoint adds to it, which is far easier to reason about than overriding downward.

motion.$comment: Every transition using these must sit inside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` guard. Motion triggers nausea and migraine for some people, and honouring the OS setting is WCAG 2.3.3.
